title: Proof memoization by goal hash
description: The simplest cache: hash the proof goal (normalized), and on a repeat, return the cached proof instead of re-proving. Interactive sessions and CI re-runs hit the same goals constantly — memoization turns repeated 'simp' calls from seconds into microseconds.
method: Normalize the goal; hash; look up the proof cache; on hit, replay the cached tactic script; on miss, prove and store.
usage: Normalize aggressively (alpha-equivalence, not string equality); bound the cache; invalidate on prover upgrades.

title: Tactic result caching
description: Tactics like 'simp' do expensive work (rewriting with hundreds of lemmas) that repeats across goals. Caching tactic results keyed by (tactic, goal shape) skips the search on repeats — the automation gets faster the more it's used.
method: Key by (tactic name + args, normalized goal); cache the resulting proof term or failure; invalidate on lemma-set changes.
usage: Cache at the tactic level for expensive tactics; watch memory on huge developments.

demo.code:
print('simp on goal shape S: cached result reused')
print('1,204 simp calls -> 312 unique -> 74% cache hit rate')

title: Counterexample cache for failed goals
description: Failed proof attempts are cached too: the goal plus its counterexample. When the same goal recurs, the cached counterexample immediately shows why it fails — no wasted solver time re-discovering unprovability, and the failure reason is documented.
method: Cache (goal -> counterexample) on failure; on recurrence, present the cached counterexample; clear when definitions change.
usage: Review cached failures periodically — a definition change may have fixed the goal.

demo.code:
print('goal G failed before: counterexample x=0 cached')
print('G recurs -> immediate: still fails, x=0 (no solver time wasted)')

title: Premise selection caching
description: Hammers spend most time selecting relevant lemmas for the ATP. Caching premise selections per goal shape — 'goals looking like this used these 40 lemmas' — skips the expensive relevance computation on repeats, making hammer calls consistently fast.
method: Cache (goal features -> lemma set); on similar goals, reuse the selection; refresh when the library changes significantly.
usage: Featurize goals robustly; refresh the cache as the library grows.

demo.code:
print('hammer premise selection: computed 8.2s -> cached 0.02s')
print('similar goal reuses 40-lemma selection')

title: Proof repair across versions
description: Library upgrades break proofs; proof repair replays cached proofs against the new library, and where they fail, searches for small patches (renamed lemmas, reordered tactics) automatically. Cached proofs become the raw material for migration, not casualties of it.
method: Replay proofs on the new version; on failure, search local patches (lemma renames, tactic fixes); keep what patches cleanly, flag the rest.
usage: Run repair as part of every upgrade; review flagged proofs promptly.

demo.code:
print('upgrade lean 4.7 -> 4.8: 2,400 proofs replayed')
print('2,310 clean, 82 auto-patched, 8 flagged for humans')

title: Cross-project proof sharing
description: Proofs are portable across projects using the same foundations: a verified sorting routine proved in one project is imported (not re-proved) by the next. Package managers for proofs (opam for Coq, reservoir for Lean) turn verification into shared infrastructure.
method: Publish verified components as packages; dependents import the proofs; version the proof packages like code.
usage: Publish general verified components; depend on proof packages instead of re-verifying.

demo.code:
print('import verified_sort (proof included)')
print('project uses it: 0 proof obligations (proof shipped with package)')

title: Distributed proof checking
description: Proof checking parallelizes beautifully: independent theorems check on separate machines. Cloud CI fans out thousands of theorems across workers, each verifying its share against the shared lemma database — full library verification in minutes, not hours.
method: Partition theorems by dependency levels; workers check their partition; a coordinator assembles the verified DAG.
usage: Partition by dependency level (level N needs level N-1 verified); cache aggressively between runs.

demo.code:
print('mathlib: 100k theorems / 64 workers -> full check 11min')
print('(single machine: 9 hours)')

title: Proof term sharing (hash-consing)
description: Proof terms share massive substructure; hash-consing stores each unique subterm once, with sharing by pointer. Developments that would use gigabytes as trees fit in memory as DAGs — the same trick Lisp and compilers use, applied to proofs.
method: Hash-cons all proof terms; equal subterms share storage; the proof is a DAG, not a tree.
usage: Enable hash-consing in the kernel; it's pure win (no soundness impact).

demo.code:
print('proof term: 2.1GB as tree -> 84MB as DAG (hash-consed)')
print('sharing: 96% of subterms shared')
